question: Are all fugitive and stack emissions accounted for in the permit application?

What are the facility's potential-to-emit figures for each criteria pollutant and total HAPs, and which PSD and Title V major-source thresholds do they cross? If below the thresholds, how close are they?
Are the estimated emissions in the permit application realistic? How do they compare to other operating plants?
Are emission factors from reputable sources like AP-42? Are the calculations correct?
Are there any assumptions made in the permit (e.g., raw material composition, control equipment efficiency)?
Are there any performance test data or manufacturer's guarantees to corroborate the assumed control efficiencies?
If this is an update to existing emissions, do the projected emissions match real recorded emissions?
Are there any portions of industrial processes which are ill-defined in the permit application?
Do the emission estimates account for startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) periods and for frequent cycling, or only steady-state full-load operation?
How many hours per year of operation do the permit limits assume, and is that capacity factor consistent with how the facility is actually expected to operate?
Are emissions from all auxiliary equipment (auxiliary boilers, emergency generators, cooling towers, firewater pumps) captured in the permit?
Does the permit include enforceable annual operating-hour or throughput caps that hold the facility to the emission levels modeled, or could it lawfully run more and emit more?

What are the estimated emissions and impacts from construction activities (diesel equipment, generators, dust, truck traffic), and are they included in the air permit or covered only under generic construction permits?

Does the air-quality modeling rely on Significant Impact Levels (SILs) to screen out a full NAAQS/increment analysis, and if so, how is that justified given the court's disapproval of SIL use in the Rise St. James/Formosa decision?
Does the NAAQS and PSD-increment modeling include background concentrations from surrounding industrial sources, or does it evaluate the facility in isolation?
What is the projected annual CO2-equivalent from all combustion and auxiliary equipment, and how was greenhouse gas BACT addressed?
Are the BACT emission limits written as enforceable, short-averaging-period limits, or as long-term averages that mask short-term spikes?
Does the additional-impacts analysis address effects on soils, vegetation, and visibility, including any impact on the nearest Class I area (e.g., Breton Wilderness)?
Is Leak Detection and Repair (LDAR) for fugitive VOC and methane emissions documented and enforceable in the permit?
What are the reliability ratings and detection limits of proposed monitoring equipment for each pollutant?
Does the monitoring plan meet EPA reference method standards or equivalent?
How frequently will independent third-party verification of emissions and control-system performance be required?
Will stack testing be required within the first year of operation to verify emission estimates, and how frequently thereafter?
Which pollutants are monitored by continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS), and which rely on periodic stack testing or emission factors instead?
What recordkeeping and public-reporting frequency applies to emissions and deviations, and will reports be posted to EDMS?
What ambient or emission exceedance levels trigger enforcement, and what sanctions (penalties, mandatory upgrades, curtailment) will apply?
How often will the agency conduct compliance inspections at the facility, and will inspection reports, notices of violation, and settlements be promptly posted to EDMS?
Will permanent community-level or fence-line air monitors be installed in nearby neighborhoods, with real-time public data for PM2.5, NO2, ozone precursors, and key toxics?

Does the permit include adaptive-management provisions to revisit emission limits, monitoring, and environmental justice analyses at each renewal in light of new science, new facilities, or changed community health indicators?
How will pollutants emitted into the air deposit into water and soil, and what problems will they cause for wildlife, including aquatic species?
Has a comprehensive cumulative impact analysis been conducted that includes all connected, adjacent, or commonly controlled facilities, or is the facility being evaluated in isolation?
How will emissions from shared infrastructure between facilities be allocated, monitored, and regulated?
What is the combined impact of all nearby facilities on ambient air quality standards?

Has a cumulative-impact analysis of air toxics (HAPs) from this facility plus nearby sources been performed, consistent with the cumulative-impact requirement recognized in the Rise St. James decision?
Has the inspection and maintenance schedule been adequately defined?
Is the Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) comprehensive and site-specific?
Is there a proper operations and maintenance plan for the wastewater treatment system?
Has the impact of temperature and chemical additives been addressed on hydrostatic test water discharge?
What surface-water and groundwater withdrawals (cooling, process, firewater) are proposed, from which sources, and what maximum daily and annual withdrawal limits are requested?
Does the cooling-water intake comply with Clean Water Act §316(b) for entrainment and impingement of fish and larvae in the source waterbody, and what intake technology is proposed?

What are the expected temperature, flow, and chemical composition (biocides, corrosion inhibitors, metals, TDS, chlorides) of cooling-water and wastewater discharges, and how do they compare to acute and chronic water-quality criteria for the receiving water?
Does the LPDES application include a mixing-zone analysis and whole-effluent toxicity (WET) testing, with a defined margin of safety for low-flow and high-temperature conditions?

How will construction and operational stormwater (including runoff from fuel storage, chemical handling, and laydown yards) be managed, and under which LPDES construction and industrial stormwater permits?
Are any deep-well injections or subsurface discharges planned (brine, process water, wastewater), and what UIC permits and geologic-integrity analyses apply?
Have all potential impacts to water quality been identified and addressed?
Are there any ways in which this permit does not comply with LAC 33:IX Chapter 11?
How will stormwater runoff be prevented from carrying pollutants into adjacent wetlands?
When was the most recent wetland delineation completed?
What is the total acreage of wetland impact, broken down by wetland type (emergent, forested, etc.)?
How was the mitigation ratio determined? Does it account for temporal losses and wetland quality/function?
What is the alternatives analysis showing why wetland impacts cannot be avoided or further minimized?
What monitoring requirements will be in place to ensure successful mitigation?

Will wetlands, riparian buffers, or other aquatic resources be filled or altered for the facility or its supporting infrastructure (pipelines, access roads), and what CWA §404/§401 and Coastal Use approvals are sought?
Does the permit fully address how coastal water quality will be impacted? Such as salt water intrusion, changes to local hydrology, and sediment transport?
What measures are proposed to minimize coastal impacts?
Has the cumulative impact analysis considered: other existing industrial facilities in the area; projected sea level rise; and coastal erosion trends?
Are there any cultural or historical resources in the project area that require protection or mitigation?
How will the project affect existing coastal restoration projects or future restoration opportunities in the area?
What long-term monitoring requirements will be in place to ensure compliance with permit conditions?
How many cubic yards of fill will be used for this project and how will that affect flooding?
Are existing drainage patterns and water regimes of the surrounding area including flow, circulation, quality, quantity, and salinity, as well as impacts on them, discussed in the permit application?
What's the extent of impacts on existing and traditional uses of the area and on future uses for which the area is suited?
Does this project demonstrate a "significant public benefit" or serve important state/regional/national interests, as required by LCRP guidelines?
Is the project consistent with Louisiana's Comprehensive Master Plan for a Sustainable Coast and any local coastal management plans?

Does the application include a complete description of total existing land use within 3 miles of the facility (residential, healthcare facilities, schools, agricultural, industrial and manufacturing, other commercial, recreational, and undeveloped) as required by LAC 33:VII.709.5?
Has the applicant submitted a current alternative site analysis that evaluates other locations, or does the analysis merely justify the site the applicant already owns?

For each requested exemption or alternative (e.g., alternative liner system), has the applicant cited the specific LAC provision and provided technical justification meeting that provision's criteria?
Has a needs assessment been performed showing that additional capacity is required in the proposed service area, or is this expansion driven solely by private commercial interest?
Does expanding the service area conflict with any regional or parish solid waste management plan?
If the service area includes out-of-state sources, what mechanism (contractual, permit condition, or otherwise) actually constrains the geographic origin of waste?
What are the most recent Surface Emissions Monitoring (SEM) results for methane and other landfill gases, and how many monitoring points exceed reportable thresholds (e.g., 500 ppm)?
If the facility currently exceeds emission limits at multiple monitoring points, what corrective actions have been taken and what evidence demonstrates those actions are working?
Will the proposed permit increase intake of waste and therefore increase decomposition rates and emissions of H2S, methane, and VOCs? If so, by how much, and how has this been modeled?
How does projected annual tonnage in the solid waste application reconcile with projected tonnage in the facility's most recent air permit application? Are they internally consistent?
Is the current odor management plan adequate at present intake levels? How many odor complaints has the facility received in the past 12, 24, and 36 months?
Does the odor management plan account for the condition of waste upon arrival (e.g., days-old waste delivered by rail or long-haul truck vs. same-day residential pickup)?
Has LDEQ reviewed the facility's solid waste, air, and groundwater permits collectively, or are they being reviewed in isolation despite obvious interdependencies?
What landfill gas collection efficiency is being assumed, and is that efficiency supported by recent performance data at this facility?
What is the leachate generation rate at current intake, and how will it scale with the proposed increase in waste acceptance?
Where is leachate ultimately disposed (e.g., POTW, Class I injection well, on-site treatment), and does the receiving facility have sufficient permitted capacity to absorb the projected increase?
Are groundwater monitoring wells placed and sampled at a frequency sufficient to detect releases before they migrate off-site?
What is the most recent groundwater monitoring data showing for each constituent of concern, and are there any exceedances or upward trends?
Does the proposed liner system meet the performance criteria of the LAC provision being relied on, and has a qualified third party reviewed the alternative liner demonstration?
Is the proposed daily and intermediate cover plan sufficient given projected intake volumes, weather patterns, and vector control needs?
What is the working face size limit, and how will it be enforced as intake increases?
What modes of waste transport will be used (truck, rail, barge), and what is the projected tonnage by mode?
For each transport mode, where are the transfer points and how are emissions, odors, and spillage controlled at those points?
What truck-washing, tarping, and load-securement measures are required, and how will compliance be inspected?
What bird-deterrence program is in place, and what monitoring/reporting demonstrates it is actually reducing bird use of the site?
Is the financial assurance instrument (financial test, bond, trust, letter of credit) adequate to cover full closure and 30-year post-closure care costs at projected final waste volumes?
If the applicant uses a financial test, does it currently meet all of the test's criteria, and what is the contingency if it fails the test mid-permit-term?
How frequently are closure and post-closure cost estimates re-evaluated and adjusted for inflation and changes in scope?

What decommissioning, equipment-removal, soil and groundwater remediation, and site-restoration obligations apply at end of life, and are financial assurances (bond, escrow) required to guarantee them?
What is the ratio of tax revenue to public costs (infrastructure, emergency services, health impacts), taking ITEP/IDEP tax abatements and subsidies into consideration?
Does the Environmental Assessment Statement separately enumerate the social and economic benefits accruing to the public versus benefits accruing to the applicant and its customers?
Are the claimed benefits in the application contingent on permit approval, or are they activities the applicant could undertake regardless of this permit action?
Has the applicant addressed each of the IT factors (potential and real adverse environmental effects, alternative projects, alternative sites, mitigating measures) as required by Louisiana case law?
Does the EAS demonstrate that adverse environmental effects have been avoided to the maximum extent possible, as required by the first IT question?
Does the EAS evaluate alternative projects and alternative sites that would offer more environmental protection without unduly curtailing benefits, as required by the third IT question?
Does the EAS cost-benefit analysis assign a quantified value to health and environmental costs borne by nearby residents, or does it list only the benefits to the applicant and its customers?
Have property value impacts on adjacent and nearby communities been quantified and included as a social/economic cost in the cost-benefit analysis?
Does the EAS separate permanent local jobs from temporary construction jobs and weigh them against the long-term environmental and health burden?
What demonstrated local or regional need for this project's output does the application establish, as opposed to serving demand located elsewhere while the burdens stay local?
Has a cumulative impacts analysis been conducted for the already overburdened communities in the area?
How does this project's pollution burden compare to EPA environmental justice screening thresholds?
Were affected environmental justice communities meaningfully consulted during application development, beyond the required public notice?
Does the environmental review adequately analyze cumulative impacts from the concentration of industrial facilities in the region?

Has the facility been evaluated under EPA's EJScreen or a comparable environmental-justice screening tool, and what were the results — noting that the Rise St. James decision found an EJ analysis mandatory under the Louisiana Constitution for LDEQ actions?
What is the demographic composition of populations within 1, 3, and 5 miles of the facility, and how do health and pollution burdens in these communities compare to state and national averages?
Were alternative locations, technologies, or configurations considered that would reduce impacts on fence-line communities?

Has a quantitative health-risk assessment (cancer risk, non-cancer hazard indices, asthma and cardiopulmonary outcomes) been produced for nearby residents based on modeled air toxics and cumulative exposure from all local facilities?

How will impacts on sensitive subpopulations (children, the elderly, people with cardiovascular or respiratory conditions) be evaluated, and are local health-outcome data (ER visits, hospitalizations, cancer registry) being used in the decision?
Did this facility have reasonable site requirements or were the site requirements chosen to match a particular site?
Were any sites excluded for erroneous reasons?
Were any sites excluded without being mentioned at all?
Does the permit application accurately calculate the net greenhouse gas emissions over the project lifecycle, including all upstream and downstream emissions?
Has formal consultation under the Endangered Species Act been completed for all potentially affected species?

Are there threatened or endangered species, migratory birds, or critical habitat in the project area; has the site been surveyed; and what avoidance, minimization, and mitigation measures are proposed?
Has the strength and breadth of community opposition been adequately considered in the public interest review?
Have property value impacts on surrounding communities been assessed?
Is there evidence the project will actually be completed as proposed from a financial standpoint?

Does the permit applicant currently have any open lawsuits, consent decrees, or notices of violation related to: Clean Water Act or Clean Air Act violations; unauthorized discharges or emissions exceeding permitted levels; wetlands destruction or unpermitted dredge/fill activities; coastal zone management violations; failure to remediate contaminated sites; false reporting of environmental monitoring data; or a pattern of environmental non-compliance at other facilities? Are all such actions at this facility and the applicant's other facilities within the past 5 years disclosed in the application?

Is the applicant currently defending against any litigation involving: oil or chemical spills in navigable waters; maritime safety violations or vessel incidents; failure to maintain adequate spill response capabilities; violations of facility security requirements under MTSA; obstruction of navigation channels; or inadequate marine transfer operations?

Does the applicant have any pending lawsuits or unresolved violations concerning: fire code violations or inadequate fire suppression systems; improper storage or handling of hazardous materials; workplace safety incidents resulting in fatalities or serious injuries; failure to report or respond to emergency releases; process safety management violations; or inadequate emergency response planning or training?

Are there any current legal actions against the applicant related to: damage to public roads or bridges from overweight vehicles; failure to obtain proper transportation permits; traffic safety violations during construction or operations; or unpermitted work in DOTD right-of-ways?

If the proposed facility includes structures over 200 feet or is near an airport, does the applicant have any history of: violations of FAA obstruction lighting requirements; unauthorized intrusions into controlled airspace; or failure to file proper notices for crane operations?

Has the applicant or its parent/subsidiary companies been subject to any of the following within the past 5 years: criminal charges or convictions related to environmental, safety, or regulatory violations; debarment or suspension from federal or state contracts; lawsuits alleging a pattern of regulatory non-compliance; whistleblower complaints upheld by regulatory agencies; securities fraud litigation related to misrepresentation of environmental or safety compliance; or class action lawsuits from communities affected by facility operations?

Does the permit applicant currently have any open lawsuits, consent decrees, or violations related to: Coastal Use Permit violations or unpermitted activities in the coastal zone; unauthorized impacts to state water bottoms or coastal wetlands; failure to comply with coastal zone consistency requirements; violations of the State and Local Coastal Resources Management Act; unpermitted dredging, filling, or structures in coastal waters; or a pattern of non-compliance with previous coastal permits?
If this is a permit renewal, have there been fires, explosions, releases, and safety incidents at this facility in the past 10 years?
Has the applicant clearly identified the legal entity (and any parent/subsidiary relationships) that will hold the permit and be responsible for compliance?
For each open or recently-closed enforcement action, what was the root cause and what permanent corrective action has been taken?
Does a sufficient contingency plan exist for the hazards introduced at the plant within the permit application?
Is an evacuation plan in the event of chemical releases laid out in the permit application?
Are there any particular risks related to this plant which are undocumented in the permit application?
Are there any legally murky areas which would encourage blame shifting in the event of an accident?

Has the applicant provided a fire prevention and response plan, and is the local fire department equipped and trained for the specific hazards at this facility, or would it need additional training and equipment?
Are details about spill prevention, hazardous materials, and emergency plans provided for this project?
Are emergency access routes and evacuation plans properly detailed?
Is the fire suppression system adequately designed for the specific hazards present?
Has a quantitative risk assessment been conducted for catastrophic release or explosion scenarios, and is an emergency response/evacuation plan referenced in the application?
Does the risk assessment model worst-case release, rupture, explosion, and fire scenarios, with blast and thermal-radiation zones mapped relative to homes, schools, and workplaces?

What is the coordination plan with parish emergency management, fire departments, and law enforcement for shelter-in-place, evacuation, and public warning, and will it be tested with regular public drills?
How will emergency response be funded and staffed over the project's life, and does the EAS account for increased costs to parish emergency services?
Are fuel, chemical, and waste storage tanks designed with secondary containment above minimum requirements, and what is the maximum storage volume of the largest tank or tank farm?
Does the facility require a Risk Management Plan under CAA §112(r) for regulated substances, and will the RMP be available for public review?
What hazardous and non-hazardous wastes (oils, solvents, spent catalysts, filters, sludge) will be generated annually, and where will they be transported, treated, or disposed?
Are there any modifications needed to existing USACE infrastructure to accommodate this project?
Have all potential impacts to existing waterway users been evaluated?
How will this impact local aviation activity?
Is there adequate analysis of traffic patterns and potential congestion?

Does the project require a new or modified access connection to a state highway, and does the application include the required traffic, sight-distance, and turn-lane analysis for an Access Connection Permit?
Does the project comply with local land use and development regulations?
When was the most recent traffic impact study performed, and does it reflect current and projected truck volumes given any proposed expansion?
Does the traffic study account for residential subdivisions and other developments built since the previous study?
Does the LDOTD concurrence letter specifically address the proposed project scope (volume increase, expansion), or does it appear to address only routine continued operation?
Who pays for road maintenance and repairs attributable to facility-generated truck traffic — the facility or the public?
Is any portion of the facility within 10,000 feet of a runway end used by turbine-powered aircraft, or within 5 miles of a runway end that could attract hazardous bird movements (FAA Order 5200.5A)?
Has the applicant consulted with the FAA and the relevant airport operator regarding bird attraction, and have their responses been included in the public record?
At peak construction, how many workers, daily truck trips, and barge/rail movements are expected, and what are the traffic, noise, and safety impacts for nearby communities?
What enforceable permit conditions control construction dust, diesel idling, nighttime lighting, and noise, including during evenings and weekends?
How will the facility maintain compliance during extreme weather events (hurricanes, flooding)?
Does the inclement weather procedure address multi-week or multi-month closures following a major hurricane or flood event?
What is the contingency plan if the gas collection system, leachate system, or working face is rendered inoperable by a natural disaster?
If the facility loses electric or water service for an extended period, can it safely continue to operate or accept waste?
What elevation, levee protection, and flood-proofing measures are proposed, and do they reflect current FEMA flood maps, sea-level rise, and increased rainfall intensity?

Does the application include a quantitative flood, storm-surge, and hurricane risk analysis over the facility's life, including worst-case fuel, chemical, and hazardous-material release during flooding?
Are backup power and emergency shutdown systems designed to operate safely during hurricanes and extended outages without uncontrolled emissions, flaring, or spills?
Does the project add fill, structures, or vibration that stress levees or riverbanks, and has the relevant flood-protection authority performed a levee-safety or geotechnical review?
Has significant public interest been demonstrated that would warrant a public hearing under LAC 33:I.Chapter 18?
Was public notice published, and direct notice provided, in every parish/community materially affected by the proposed action — downwind and downriver — not just the host parish?
Are all attachments referenced in the Fact Sheet and approval letter actually accessible to the public on EDMS for the entire public comment period?
If the applicant submitted supplemental information after the original application date, has the public been given a meaningful opportunity to review and comment on those supplements?
Will written responses to all substantive public comments be issued and made part of the administrative record before final permit action?
Will the agency hold accessible public hearings (convenient time and location, language access, virtual option)?

Will all applications, modeling files, health analyses, and draft permit conditions be posted to EDMS, and can the public obtain modeling inputs and outputs in native electronic format rather than PDF only?
Has the applicant provided evidence that the project will actually reduce emissions rather than increase them as recent analyses suggest?
Has a comprehensive geological survey been conducted to identify all fault lines beneath the CO2 plume that could be affected by CO2 injection?
Have all abandoned oil and gas wells in the vicinity been properly evaluated for their potential to serve as CO2 escape pathways?
What is the risk assessment for induced seismicity from high-pressure CO2 injection?
Has groundwater contamination risk from CO2 injection been adequately assessed?
Were all reasonable alternatives to meet energy objectives thoroughly evaluated?
What safety measures are proposed to prevent incidents similar to the Satartia, Mississippi CO2 pipeline rupture?
What is the evacuation radius for potential CO2 pipeline failures?
How will first responders be trained for CO2 pipeline emergencies?

Does the BACT analysis evaluate lower-emitting alternatives to combustion turbines (e.g., solar-plus-storage, demand response, or a smaller turbine fleet), or does it assume the turbine design and only compare add-on controls?

What NOx, CO, VOC, PM2.5, SO2, and formaldehyde emission limits are set as BACT, and how do they compare to the most stringent limits in EPA's RBLC clearinghouse for recently permitted comparable plants?
Under the Acid Rain permit, what are the SO2 and NOx allowance allocations, and does the facility hold or must it acquire sufficient allowances without increasing regional emissions?
What is the source, route, and pressure of the natural gas supply, and what are the air-quality and safety implications of any associated new pipeline or metering infrastructure?

What new pipelines, compressor stations, metering stations, and high-pressure gas lines are required to serve the facility, where will they be located, and which agencies are reviewing their safety and environmental impacts?

Does the EAS evaluate non-fossil alternatives (renewables plus storage, demand-side management, transmission upgrades) capable of meeting the same load with lower emissions, as the third IT factor requires?

Do the maximum hourly emission rates, multiplied by the hours of operation the application itself assumes, exceed the annual permitted tonnage for any pollutant? If so, the hourly and annual figures describe two mutually exclusive facilities — which one is enforceable, and what permit condition reconciles them?

Are emissions from activities designated insignificant, de minimis, or authorized under a general condition excluded from the emission totals published in the public notice? Quantify the excluded emissions and state them as a percentage of the noticed figures — and check whether the same document elsewhere declares that no such activities exist.

Do any emission figures, throughput assumptions, or operating-hour assumptions disagree between documents in the noticed package — or between two places in the same document? For each disagreement, which figure governs, and does any enforceable permit condition fix it?

Where the emission calculations take credit for a control device's destruction or removal efficiency, does the permit impose every operating limit on which the governing regulation conditions that credit — or only some of them? (For flares, 40 CFR 60.18 conditions the credit on net heating value AND exit velocity; a permit setting only the heating value licenses operation well outside the envelope the assumed efficiency depends on.)

Is the throughput, production rate, or material quantity that generated every emission figure in the application actually written into the permit as an enforceable cap — or does it appear only in narrative and calculation worksheets while the permit limits tonnage alone?

Does the application supply discrete source coordinates and discrete stack parameters, or does it give ranges, "varies", or "TBD"? Dispersion models require single values; where the inputs are ranges or undetermined, no compliance demonstration can have been performed on them, and the agency's ambient-air finding rests on nothing but the annual tonnage.

Did agency technical staff raise a modeling, ambient-standard, or emission-rate concern during review? If so, obtain the internal correspondence and establish how it was resolved — by analysis, or by revising the applicant's inputs downward until the concern disappeared.

Do the documents in the agency's electronic docket match their index descriptions? Open each one rather than trusting the index — misindexed entries can conceal whether any public comment has in fact been filed, and can hide records of failed notice.

If the application was revised during technical review, does the noticed package clearly identify which version governs — or does it carry the superseded narrative alongside the revised figures, leaving the public unable to tell what is actually being authorized? Does the public notice disclose that the figures were revised, and why?

Is there evidence in the record that individually mailed notices were returned undeliverable? How many were returned, what did the agency do to correct the mailing list, and does a returned notice satisfy the direct-notice requirement?

Is the permit classified consistently across the public notice, the draft permit, and the approval letter — including permit number and permit type? Where the notice says "minor source" but the permit says "synthetic minor", the public is not told that the source would be major but for federally enforceable limits, nor how those limits are actually verified.

Did the applicant receive a working draft and a private remark round before public notice? If so, is the completed technical-review worksheet capturing those remarks actually in the public record, as the notice represents — or only the blank form?

Does the application identify a specific location for the source, or does it request authorization at "any location" within a described area? If location is undetermined, establish how any location-dependent analysis — dispersion modeling, ambient standard compliance, cumulative impact, environmental-justice screening, setbacks from receptors — could have been performed, and whether the agency performed it for even one location.

Does the permit contain an enforceable condition constraining where the source may operate? Check whether that condition is self-referential — a requirement to obtain approval before relocating "outside the approved locations" is unenforceable where no approved location is defined anywhere in the permit or application.

Where a standing permit replaces case-by-case variances or event-specific authorizations, what location-specific agency review is lost, and what replaces it? Is any advance notice to the agency, to local officials, or to nearby residents required before an event at a given location?

Are the source's physical parameters — stack height, diameter, exit velocity, flow rate, exit temperature — specified as discrete values or as ranges? Does any permit condition bind the operator to a point within those ranges, and were the emission calculations performed at the worst case within them?

How many events per year, and how many hours per event, does the emissions basis assume? Is either an enforceable permit condition? Check the maximum-hourly and annual-total assumptions against each other — campaigns frequently find the two computed on different event durations.

What operating history supports the assumed event frequency — prior variances, authorizations, or event logs — and how current is it? Compare the applicant's disclosed history against its own statement of need; a disclosure that stops years before the application contradicts a claim that authorizations are sought "currently" and "each time" the activity is necessary.

For a source with no fixed location, what monitoring, recordkeeping, or reporting would let the agency or a nearby resident determine what was emitted, where, and when? Establish whether compliance rests on measurement or solely on the operator recomputing the same emission factors used to set the limit.

Does the public notice describe the geographic scope consistently with what the permit authorizes? Where a notice calls a facility statewide but places notice in only some parishes, determine whether the authorization reaches communities that received no notice, and whether any broader request in the application was ever withdrawn.

Does the AOR investigation's stated search radius match the radius used for any separate "wells within X miles" survey elsewhere in the application (e.g., orphan or abandoned-well tables), and does the AOR explicitly state whether it was delineated using the CO2 plume, the pressure front, or both? For any wells identified in a nearby-wells survey that fall within the larger of those two extents, does the application reconcile them against a "no artificial penetrations" / "no corrective action needed" conclusion?

Does the modeled pressure front — as opposed to the free-phase CO2 plume — extend beyond the operator's leased or pore-space-rights-controlled acreage? If so, what consent, notice, or additional pore-space rights has the operator obtained for the acreage outside its control, and does the application's containment-assurance language address the pressure front specifically or only the plume?

Does the application's fault-slip-potential or induced-seismicity analysis describe project faults as "transmissive" in a pressure-communication sense, while a separate AOR or containment section asserts that no geologic feature allows fluid movement out of the injection zone? If both claims appear, does the application reconcile the two uses of "transmissive"/"movement," or are they left as apparently conflicting technical claims?

Beyond a general regional seismic-hazard or land-loss citation, has the applicant conducted or commissioned site-specific modeling of surface subsidence induced by the project's own reservoir pressure buildup — particularly where the injection zone lies within a fault-bounded structural block or beneath a wetland or coastal setting?

For each required Class VI financial-assurance cost category (corrective action, well plugging, PISC/site closure, emergency and remedial response), which financial instrument has the applicant selected, and is that instrument among the state Class VI rule's named base instruments for that category, or does it require a discretionary/catch-all approval? What is the state's default PISC monitoring period, and does the chosen instrument's stated policy term, renewal, and continuation provisions match that duration?

Where sections of the ERRP, QASP, or other Class VI technical plans are redacted from the public application, does the application or agency cite a specific statutory exemption (trade secret, critical infrastructure security, or other) for withholding risk-scenario narratives, monitoring instrumentation, or detection-limit methodology — as distinct from genuinely sensitive details like exact coordinates or security countermeasures? Do the redacted sections track cleanly to a defensible exemption category, or do they encompass information not obviously covered by a trade-secret or security rationale?

Where a single Class VI site application covers multiple wells under one or a small number of linked application/site numbers, does the state's public tracking system surface a distinct row for each well, or only for the lead/primary well? For wells not independently surfaced, what public notice mechanism, if any, applies to them individually?

Does any NAAQS or PSD-increment compliance table show a modeled total concentration exceeding the applicable standard while the narrative on the same page, or elsewhere in the application, asserts compliance? If so, obtain the culpability analysis identifying the contributing source(s), the receptor location, and the modeled hour/date of the exceedance.

Do the meteorological station, meteorological data years, and upper-air station actually used in the dispersion modeling match those specified in the agency-approved modeling protocol? For any deviation, was an amended modeling protocol submitted and approved before the modeling was run?

Does the arithmetic in the emissions offsets table match the ratio stated elsewhere in the application, or has the NNSR applicability/major-modification threshold been subtracted from the net emissions increase as a deductible before offsets are calculated, understating the true offset obligation?

Comparing the noticed application against earlier versions submitted to the agency during technical review, were any analyses (e.g., cumulative-impact, environmental-justice, health-risk) present in an earlier draft but absent from the noticed version? If so, does the record give a reason for the removal?

Was the permit application processed on an expedited or fast-track review schedule? Was a fee cap or expedited-review fee requested, and how does the requested or targeted decision date compare to the public notice date and the close of the comment period?

Do all activity numbers referenced in the administrative record appear on the public notice, or were any prerequisite approvals (e.g., a preliminary determination, a related permit modification) processed under a separate activity number that was never itself noticed?
Does the application's land-use inventory or facility siting analysis identify churches, cemeteries, and church-owned parcels within the stated survey radius?
Are places of worship carried as sensitive receptors — alongside schools and hospitals — in the dispersion, noise, odor, traffic, and emergency-evacuation analyses supporting the application?

Does any property line adjoin a structure currently used, and used as a church prior to the submittal of the permit application, triggering the 300-foot buffer zone under LAC 33:VII.709.B.3.a (or the parallel provision at §717.B.3.a or §719.B.3.a, depending on facility class) rather than the lesser buffer otherwise applicable to this facility class; if a reduction is claimed, is the notarized affidavit from every landowner within the buffer in the record and recorded in the parish's mortgage and conveyance records; and if the pre-April 1, 2010 exemption is invoked, does the facility actually qualify — an existing facility, a closed portion, or an expansion within the already-permitted disposal or processing area — rather than being a new unit characterized as an expansion?

LAC 33:VII.709.A.5 (and the parallel §717.A.5 / §719.A.6) requires the 3-mile land-use description to include, but not be limited to, residential, health-care facilities and schools, agricultural, industrial and manufacturing, other commercial, recreational, and undeveloped uses — does the applicant's inventory also identify places of worship and cemeteries within that radius, consistent with the provision's own non-exclusive list?

Was the Area of Potential Effects drawn to include the parish church, its cemetery, and congregation access routes, or only the construction footprint, and were affected congregations and descendant communities invited or admitted as consulting parties under 36 CFR 800.2(c)(5) and 800.3(f)(3)?
Has SHPO concurrence on the Area of Potential Effects and any identified historic properties been obtained, and is that correspondence in the public record?

Does the record address the Louisiana Unmarked Human Burial Sites Preservation Act (R.S. 8:671-681) — is the project area known or suspected to contain human remains, or immediately adjacent to property known to have burials?
Were any Division of Archaeology or SHPO communications concerning possible unmarked burials excluded from the noticed application package?
Will construction, haul routes, or facility operations obstruct access to a cemetery or place of worship, including on All Saints Day and other customary decoration days?

Does the public-interest review give the "due consideration" 33 CFR 320.4(e) requires to the "recognized historic, cultural, scenic, conservation, recreational or similar values" attached to affected churches and cemeteries, and does the record show that consideration was actually made rather than merely reciting the factor?

Is the facility located in, or within 1,000 feet of, an archaeological site or historic site under LAC 33:VII.709.A.7 (or the parallel §717.A.7 / §719.A.4), and were the resulting isolation and documentation requirements addressed?
